authoring: React-owned metadata for the released low-level Input export

intentAndPurpose.intent: Low-level single-line text entry control. Use standalone only when a visible label, helper text, and validation chrome are not required; otherwise use InputField.

requires: an accessible name through aria-label or an owning InputField label

interactionBehavior.summary: Input's focus indicator is NOT the system focus halo. Focus promotes the container's border to `--Stroke-XL` in the role's Tinted colour with `outline: none`, and it is keyed off `:focus-within` rather than `:focus-visible` — so a mouse click paints exactly the same indicator a keyboard focus does. A padding-compensation variable absorbs the extra border width so the field does not shift when it gains focus. There is also no filled state: `data-filled` / `data-dirty` / `data-touched` are never styled, so only the value vs placeholder text colour distinguishes an empty field from a typed one.
hover: The container background tints on hover, guarded by `@media (hover: hover)` so a touch tap leaves no stuck fill.
Every hover rule is qualified `:not(:focus-within)`, so hover never fights the focus stroke once the field is focused.
A read-only field re-asserts its own resting background on hover instead of tinting, so it does not look actionable.
focus: No focus halo. The container border grows to `--Stroke-XL` in the role's Tinted colour and the native outline is removed.
Keyed off `:focus-within`, not `:focus-visible` — clicking with a mouse shows the same stroke as tabbing in.
Geometry is invariant: an idle padding-adjust variable drops to 0 as the border thickens, so the field and its content do not move.
At `attention="high"` a transparent XL border is pre-reserved at rest for the same reason.
Focusing anywhere inside — including a slot button — lights the whole container, because the trigger is `:focus-within`.
keyboard: The control is a real `<input>`, so all native text-editing keys, caret movement, and selection behave normally; key handlers you pass are forwarded verbatim.
Interactive `end` / `end2` slot content stays in the tab order (`pointer-events: auto`), so a trailing clear or reveal button is its own tab stop after the field.
selected: There is NO filled/dirty state: `data-filled`, `data-dirty` and `data-touched` are never styled. Only the value vs placeholder text colour differs.
Invalid state OUTRANKS focus — the error stroke is re-asserted under `:focus-within`, so focusing an invalid field does not hide the error colour.
An invalid field keeps `--Stroke-XL` even at rest, so it stays visibly flagged when unfocused.

Read-only repaints rather than dims: at medium attention it becomes a filled `--Neutral-Minimal` with a transparent stroke; at high attention it goes ghost with `--Neutral-Stroke-Low`. The caret is `cursor: default`.
disabled: The container dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` (overridable via `--Input-disabledOpacity`) and sets `user-select: none`.

`cursor: not-allowed` IS observable here, unlike most disabled controls: the cursor sits on the container, which stays hit-testable, and only the inner control and the start/end slot groups take `pointer-events: none`.
Hover tinting is suppressed, so a disabled field never reacts to the pointer.
touch: Hover tinting never applies on touch-only devices; the focus stroke is the entire response to a tap.
Sizes XS (24px) and S (32px) are BELOW the 44px minimum touch target — pick M (40px) or L (48px) for touch-primary surfaces, or extend the hit area yourself.
